spec.title: PROP-073 — Exact publication subjects and effect authority
spec.p: This document governs a future publication operation. The current distribution bundle, platform fragment and aggregate contracts remain the input evidence defined by [PROP-019](PROP-019-version-manager.xml#instances). The format rules of [PROP-044](PROP-044-change-native-formats.xml#root) and the lifecycle ownership rules of [PROP-054](PROP-054-lifecycle-and-extensions.xml#root) still apply. A prepared plan is data for inspection and authorization. It grants no remote write, and this proposal does not authorize a public Git push or release.

p.PUBLICATION-EXACT-SUBJECT-LAW: The publication owner constructs one canonical subject from an explicitly selected clean committed source commit and tree, a separate SHA-256 and byte-length witness for Cargo.lock read from that same commit, the exact mutable SemVer target, and the complete supported platform set. For each target it binds one platform fragment and its exact distribution bundle, raw bootstrap executable, embedded component digests and sizes, source archive digest, size and tree OID, and the fragment's version, commit, tree and target. It also binds the aggregate manifest and the committed installer asset bytes by name, media type, byte length and SHA-256, and names the effective smoke-policy identity and exact evidence or typed unavailability. Every input is validated against its existing strict distribution contract. A missing, duplicate, foreign-target, stale or unverified bundle refuses an apply-ready subject; a matching filename, version or source commit alone never proves its bytes. In the active next campaign the target version is 1.1.0 and mutable: replacing that version's authorized bytes does not increment it, while 1.0.0 remains the already-used predecessor. A changed source tree, committed lock witness, target set, fragment, bundle, installer or smoke evidence changes the subject identity or refuses construction.

p.PUBLICATION-SUBJECT-DIGEST-LAW: The subject's epoch-one SHA-256 is over a distinct publication-subject domain tag and unambiguous ordered tagged frames. Frames include explicit schema/recipe identity, target repository identity, source commit and tree, committed lock witness, version and mutability, complete target count and canonical target order, each named asset's type, size and digest, and smoke-policy/evidence identity. A collection encodes its count before elements and an optional value encodes presence separately from an empty value. Text uses exact validated UTF-8; integers use fixed-width unsigned big-endian bytes; binary digests use raw decoded bytes. Input declaration order does not choose target order. A digest over only the rendered manifest JSON, a remote tag spelling or a package version is not this subject identity.

p.PUBLICATION-EFFECT-PLAN-LAW: A pure planner consumes the validated local subject, an explicitly selected destination owner/repository and a separately captured remote observation. It lists every intended mutation in ordered partitions: create an absent tag ref or retain its exact observed commit ref; replace a known prior draft release by its exact ID and complete asset inventory, then create the new draft; for each supported target replace its bundle, bootstrap and fragment assets by canonical names and exact observed asset IDs; replace the aggregate and three installer assets; and, only when separately authorized, change the verified draft's visibility and latest-release posture. Existing release/tag identity, draft state, source commit, asset names, IDs, sizes and digests, including explicit absence, are plan inputs, not facts inferred after approval. Replacing a draft deletes the old release before a new draft is created: old asset IDs belong only to that deletion, while assets in the new draft start absent. A cleanup step for assets observed only after upload requires a new bounded observation and plan rather than invented prior IDs. Deleting a release implicitly deletes its assets, so a prior release whose complete asset inventory cannot be observed has an unknown effect set and refuses an apply-ready plan. Cleanup of temporary assets is also an explicit delete partition, never a hidden preparation step. The plan names each replacement's prior ID and intended successor identity, dependency order and recovery prerequisite. Read-only remote discovery occurs outside the pure planner; plan construction itself performs no filesystem or network write, creates no tag or release, and loads no credential.

p.PUBLICATION-PLAN-DIGEST-LAW: The epoch-one effect-plan SHA-256 has a publication-plan domain tag separate from the subject digest. Ordered frames bind the subject digest, target owner/repository, requested operation and visibility posture, every partition and its exact remote precondition, absent/present markers, replaced release/tag/asset IDs and observed generation, intended names and byte digests, smoke policy and recovery prerequisites. Changing a target, remote generation, replacement ID, selected operation or asset changes the plan identity. Immediately before each remote effect the owner reobserves its stated preconditions; drift refuses before that effect. Where a provider offers no atomic compare-and-swap across separate remote objects, a race after reobservation is reported as partial or uncertain with the landed partition recorded, never as a no-effects refusal.

p.PUBLICATION-SMOKE-POLICY-LAW: The selected smoke policy has its own versioned identity, ordered required probes, platform scope and applicability rule. For each probe the owner records passed, failed, skipped or unavailable separately, with the tested subject/asset digest, tool or runner identity and bounded evidence reference. A skip, unavailable runner, missing target, stale result or test against different bytes never becomes passed by omission. The pure plan states which results are required before an apply-ready or publish-ready verdict; a policy may explicitly allow a skip only by a named rule bound into the plan identity. Current optional build gates are evidence only when they ran against the same pinned source and produced bundle bytes. This clause defines evidence and readiness, not permission to run a costly or remote check automatically.

authority.title: 4. Plan, approval and journal remain different

PUBLICATION-JOURNAL-BOUNDARY.title: No effect from a plan alone

p.PUBLICATION-JOURNAL-BOUNDARY-LAW: The prepared subject and effect plan are inspectable data. Mode A approval and any later explicitly enabled Mode B policy evaluate the same exact plan but are separate authority. Neither an approved plan, a dry-run result, an existing release, a previous successful publication, nor an installed operation descriptor authorizes public publication by itself. A protected machine submission additionally requires the publication owner's own durable pre-effect journal under the M-16-C.2 reservation fence: it records exact plan and remote preconditions before the first write, tracks each landed, pending or uncertain partition, and retains the final or recovery-required outcome. A post-publication manifest or registry fact is evidence of what landed, not a substitute for that journal. Until the owner can recover a lost response without replaying an uncertain remote write, protected machine publication remains unavailable. This proposal neither creates such a journal nor grants a public Git push or release.
